about: A cave-adventure sequel: the returning hero at the foot of an endless stair, told in a dream to seek a silver-haired old man for a final test, with a lantern, a sword stuck in a rock, and dark passages.

done.why: I sampled the writing for a few turns and left early; nothing was resolved.

moments.note: Lantern described as an old friend who followed you somewhere it would rather not be.
Sword hilt worn to the shape of your own hand.
The grue warning in the dark, a nod to older games.

wished: Find a way to free the sword
Explore much more of the caverns

lines.line: It has the look of an old friend who has followed you somewhere it would rather not have come.
lines.why: Gives an object character in one sentence.

lines.line: a hilt worn to the shape of a hand, which, when you close yours on it, turns out to be yours.
lines.why: An intimate image that suggests fate.

fun.why: Pleasant start, but I played too briefly to judge.

engagement.why: The dream opening and the sword create curiosity.

difficulty.why: Little resistance in the few turns played.

interestingness.why: A callback sequel with a final-test frame and a sword in the stone.

prose.why: Object descriptions are specific and feeling; room text is solid and functional.
